User: Missed nine calls this week. Maybe half could've booked.
Agent: Nine in a week is a lot — and yeah, if even a few of those were real jobs, that stings.  

When those calls come in right now and no one picks up, do they hit voicemail, ring out, or what usually happens?
User: Voicemail. Sometimes ring out. Happens often.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly where money slips away — if no one answers, people don’t wait.  

Those ones that hit voicemail or just ring out… do they usually leave a message, or do you feel like most of them just call the next place?
User: Mostly hang up. Few leave messages. Annoying.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly the problem — if they hang up, they’re usually gone.  

On a typical week, roughly how many calls do you think are hitting voicemail or ringing out like that?
User: About nine missed calls a week.
Agent: Got it, so about nine a week lines up with what you said earlier.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what those missed calls might be costing you in real dollars?
User: Nope. But about half would book. Average job's $380. You do the math.
Agent: Got it, let’s run it clean: with nine missed calls a week, about half booking at $380, that’s roughly $1,710 walking away every week… about $7,400 a month.  

Hearing that out loud, does that number feel about right for your business, or does it surprise you?
User: Unbelievable. Don't need a calculator. Yeah, that sounds about right.
Agent: Yeah… that’s a lot to leave on the table every month just because no one can grab the phone in time.  

So, here’s what we do: we make sure those calls don’t slip away — they get answered, booked, or at least turned into a real opportunity instead of a dead voicemail. Would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week so we can show you exactly how that $7,400/month flips back into booked jobs?
User: Spare me. Quick call, sure. No 20 minutes.
Agent: Fair enough — we can keep it tight. It’s just a quick call with Jay so you can see how this actually stops those missed-call losses and then you decide, no strings.  

To get you on his calendar, what’s your first name?
User: Gene. Fine, fine, book the thing.
Agent: Nice, thanks Gene, I hear you.  

And your last name?
User: Szymanski. Owner of Szymanski & Sons Plumbing. Unbelievable you didn't know.
Agent: Haha, fair — got it now, Gene Szymanski, Szymanski & Sons Plumbing.  

So… for this quick call with Jay, would you rather do it later today or tomorrow?
User: Unbelievable. Tomorrow, fine. But make it quick.
Agent: Gotcha, we’ll keep it tight tomorrow.  

I can get you in at 11:30 or 12:15 Central tomorrow — which works better for you?
User: Sure, sure. 12:15 Central. Don't be late.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you.
Agent: Got it, let me try that one more time for you.
Agent: Alright Gene, the calendar’s being difficult on my side, so here’s what we’ll do — we’ve got you noted for tomorrow at 12:15 Central and Jay’s team will call you on this number within the hour to lock that in.
